paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the LORD reigns, and that is GOOD news. The psalm says clouds and darkness surround Him, but "righteousness and justice are His throne’s foundation." (Psalm 97:2) So the One in charge of everything is not shaky, not moody, and not making it up as He goes. Even when you can't see the whole picture, you can trust who is sitting on that throne.

That's why the psalm tells the earth to rejoice. (Psalm 97:1) Mountains melt like wax before Him, and idols can't do a thing, so every other thing we lean on is smaller than we think. (Psalm 97:5, 7) The singer says it plainly: "You are exalted far above all gods." (Psalm 97:9) I leaned on plenty of things that couldn't hold me up, and I'm telling you, it is a relief to know who really can.

So what do we do with a King like that? "Hate evil, O you who love the LORD!" The reason is that "He preserves the souls of His saints; He delivers them from the hand of the wicked." (Psalm 97:10) Then comes the invitation: "Rejoice in the LORD, you righteous ones, and praise His holy name." (Psalm 97:12) Baker, you don't have to carry the world today. Look at who reigns, and let the gladness win.
